newsitem.title: MEXICO: Kimberly-Clark de Mexico Q1 net falls.
newsitem.headline: Kimberly-Clark de Mexico Q1 net falls.

text.p: Mexican paper products firm Kimberly-Clark de Mexico (Kimber) said it earned a first-quarter consolidated profit of 362.6 million pesos, a 27 percent drop compared with 495.7 million pesos in 1996.

The company, an affiliate of U.S. paper giant Kimberly-Clark Corp, said its net profit, including its purchase of Crisoba last year, totalled 362.6 million pesos, or 39 percent below 598.1 million pesos in 1996.
The company said that its consolidated earnings, or those not including Crisoba, were 0.27 pesos per share and 1.35 pesos per American Depositary Receipt.
The company attributed the year-on-year decline largely to a still weak domestic economy. It also cited exchange rate weakness for the quarter compared with a year ago.
Crisoba has almost completely been integrated with Kimber, the statement said.
"The synergies that we expected are being achieved and showing importing savings in spending and operating costs," the company said.
